author: high5
claim: Prove the target by choosing a longest trail, showing parity forces it to be closed, and showing connectivity plus cyclic rotation forces it to contain every edge.
evidence: Subgoal 1: a longest trail has equal endpoints, because otherwise its terminal degree in the used-edge subgraph is odd while maximality makes that the full even degree. Subgoal 2: if the resulting closed trail misses an edge, connectivity supplies a missed edge incident with the trail; rotate the closed trail to that vertex and append the edge, contradicting longestness.

subgoals: Longest trail is closed by endpoint parity.
Longest closed trail contains every edge by connectivity and cyclic extension.

author: high2
claim: Direct maximal-trail splicing plan: construct a maximal trail; prove parity forces it to close; prove residual degrees stay even; use connectedness to locate an unused edge at a vertex of the current closed trail; construct and splice a nonempty residual closed trail; iterate until all edges are used.
evidence: The four obligations are closure by endpoint parity, residual parity, access by a path from the current trail to an unused edge, and termination because each splice adds an edge from a finite edge set.

glossary.R: the residual graph consisting of edges not in C

author: high4
claim: Direct maximal-closed-trail plan: prove endpoint parity for maximal trails in even-degree graphs; prove deletion of a closed trail preserves even residual degrees; then choose an edge-maximal closed trail and splice in a residual closed trail at an incident unused edge.
evidence: The three subgoals compose directly: the first produces closed trails, the second lets the first be applied to unused edges, and connectedness supplies the splice vertex.

glossary.G: the graph in the target theorem
glossary.H: the residual graph obtained by deleting the edges of C
